slides.title: Crude Oil: A Complex Mixture of Hydrocarbons
slides.text:
Crude Oil: A Complex Mixture of Hydrocarbons
Origin, Chemical Foundations & the Alkane Homologous Series

1. A Finite Fossil Fuel
- Formed over millions of years from the fossilised remains of ancient marine biomass (principally plankton).
- Buried under thick seabed mud without oxygen (anaerobic conditions).
- Classified as a FINITE RESOURCE: extracted much faster than it is formed; it cannot be naturally replaced once depleted.
- It is a mixture of thousands of distinct organic molecules not chemically bonded together.

2. What is a Hydrocarbon?
- A molecule formed of Hydrogen and Carbon ONLY.
- Carbon valency: Carbon has 4 outer electrons, so it must form 4 covalent bonds.
- Hydrogen valency: Hydrogen has 1 electron, so it forms 1 covalent bond.
- Marking Trap: Saying 'contains hydrogen and carbon' drops marks — you must state ONLY!

3. The Alkane Family
- General Formula: CnH2n+2
- Saturated molecules: contain only single C-C bonds (maximum hydrogens attached).
- Progression: Gases (C1-C4) -> Liquids (C5-C12) -> Waxes & Solids (C16+)
- The Separation Imperative: Crude oil itself is unusable directly because its molecules have wildly differing boiling points, viscosities, and flammabilities. It must be separated!

slides.title: Molymod Challenge: Building Alkanes & Alkenes
slides.text:
Molymod Challenge: Building Alkanes & Alkenes
Hands-On Molecular Modelling Workshop

Molymod Component Specification:
- Carbon (black sphere, 4 tetrahedral holes, 4 covalent bonds)
- Hydrogen (white sphere, 1 hole, 1 covalent bond)
- Single bond (rigid grey link for C-C, C-H)
- Double bond (two flexible curved links for C=C)
- Golden Lab Rule: No empty holes! Every Carbon must have 4 bonds; every Hydrogen must have 1 bond.

Challenge 1: Saturated Alkanes (CnH2n+2)
- Build Methane (CH4) and Ethane (C2H6).
- Build Propane (C3H8) by inserting a 3rd carbon.
- Tactile Observation: Carbon backbone forms a 3D zigzag with 109.5° tetrahedral angles—it is not flat!
- Saturated: all C-C bonds are single bonds; no more hydrogens can be added.

Challenge 2: Unsaturated Alkenes (CnH2n)
- Build Ethene (C2H4) using two flexible curved links for the C=C double bond.
- Tactile Test: Try to twist the C=C bond. Notice it is locked and rigid (planar geometry, 120° bond angle).
- Bromine Water Test: The reactive double bond breaks open—turning orange bromine water colourless!
- Unsaturated: contains at least one double covalent bond (C=C).

Challenge 3: Extension — Structural Isomers (C4H10)
- Using exactly 4 Carbons & 10 Hydrogens, build 2 completely different molecules!
- Structure A: Straight-chain Butane (CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3, bp -0.5°C).
- Structure B: Branched 2-Methylpropane (CH(CH3)3, bp -11.7°C).
- Key Concept: Same molecular formula, different structural arrangements = Structural Isomers.
- Property Link: Branched chains pack less tightly, resulting in weaker intermolecular forces and lower boiling points.

metadata.topic: Molymod physical molecular modeling of alkanes, alkenes, and structural isomers
keyPillars: Molymod valency rules (Carbon 4 bonds, Hydrogen 1 bond)
Alkenes unsaturated planar rigid C=C double bond (120°)

academicReferences.relevance: Demonstrates that physical ball-and-stick manipulation directly improves 3D spatial understanding of molecular geometries.
